video.title: He Built This Business in One Weekend for $40

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Spencer, who built a custom pet portrait business (transcribed as 'Printer Pet') over one weekend on Shopify for about $40, using print-on-demand fulfilment and commissioned artists in the Philippines. It launched in November 2019, took off with COVID pet adoption and Etsy, and hit just over $1M revenue in its first full year with over $800k in November-December alone; sales are highly seasonal and now declining. Chris advises fresh-creative Facebook ads (his Texas Snacks gets 10x ROAS at $500/day), testing whether customers actually prefer cheaper AI art, and live selling on Whatnot/TikTok Live. He also pitches Nano Banana side ideas: AI landscaping mock-up leads for landscapers and $1-per-photo AI virtual staging for listing agents. Transcript is Whisper (mis-heard names and numbers).

ideas.name: Custom pet portrait print-on-demand store
ideas.one_liner: Customers upload pet photos; offshore artists draw stylised portraits, printed and shipped by print-on-demand partners as posters, frames, canvases or digital files.
ideas.business_model: One-off product sales (DTC Shopify and Etsy)
ideas.customer: Pet owners and gift buyers (about 60% gifts: memorials, new puppies, birthdays)
ideas.problem: Want a personalised keepsake of a pet
ideas.offer: Hand-drawn pet portraits in several styles, up to five pets, frames, backgrounds, rush queue and other upsells; an automated 'vogue' style needs no artist

pricing.notes: Free shipping absorbed; gross margins 60-70% overall, 40-50% on framed portraits.

acquisition_channels.details: Etsy listings and Etsy ads (pay-per-click, $1,000/day budget but often only $100/day spent outside Q4).

quote.text: I put the products on Etsy and that's where everything really just hockey-sticked and blew up.
quote.speaker: Spencer

acquisition_channels.details: Basic Facebook ads from month two; scaled down once Etsy worked.
Launch via personal Facebook posts, Instagram engagement pods and paying pet pages ($20-50) for posts; Pinterest worked well.
Email list of about 24,000 with pruning flows.

ideas.delivery: Overseas commissioned artists (80 at peak, mostly Philippines) draw portraits; print-on-demand/screen-printing partners print, frame and ship for a flat rate; one employee grades files for the automated style.
unit_economics_claims: Over $800k revenue in Nov-Dec 2020; first full year just over $1M
ideas.startup_cost: About $30-40 (Shopify plan) built over one weekend

acquisition.how: Etsy search/ads and Meta ads run inbound; creative refresh can be agent-made.

onboarding.how: Self-serve checkout with photo upload and options.

delivery.how: AI image models could replace artists (they already automate one style); printing/shipping is outsourced POD; human QA of files.

support.how: AI agents can handle revision back-and-forth; some edge cases need humans.

uk_applicability.notes: UK POD printers and Etsy UK make it identical; strong UK pet gifting market.

tactics.name: Weekend print-on-demand launch
steps: Spot a product style working for a competitor (Renaissance pet portraits) and adapt it
Build a Shopify store over a weekend with YouTube tutorials and Canva
Outsource art via Fiverr/Upwork and fulfilment to print-on-demand
Launch with personal social posts around Black Friday
Add Facebook ads in month two and Etsy in month three

quote.text: I knew that I could start up for close to nothing
quote.speaker: Spencer

tactics.name: Multi-step customiser checkout to raise AOV
steps: Step 1 choose style and number of pets (up to 5)
Step 2 frame, size, background with paid upgrades rounded up (e.g. $8 cost frame sold for $10)
Offer a paid skip-the-queue rush option
Final step photo upload, name, font, halo, artist notes
Result: AOV up 20%

tactics.name: Creative-volume Facebook ads
steps: Use broad targeting / CBO and let Meta find the audience
Film lots of simple employee videos with products (10 seconds to 10 minutes)
Put spend behind winners
Replace creative when performance dips after 1-2 weeks
Optionally test many AI-avatar UGC ads with HeyGen

quote.text: You need more creative. You need to test more things.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Survey price vs human-made preference
steps: Show customers a $90 human-drawn and a $65 AI version side by side
Ask which they'd buy
Decide whether the human-art differentiator is worth the margin

tactics.name: Live auction to drive store traffic
steps: Prepare prints of the most common breeds in ~20 styles
Auction them on TikTok Live/Whatnot
Use the show to send viewers to the website

quote.text: And do an auction like for a eight by 12 or whatever for the drawing style.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Spy on competitors in Meta Ad Library
steps: Regularly review competitor ads (e.g. Aston Willow) in the Meta Ad Library
Copy what works and test it

warnings.warning: Etsy ads can't guarantee spend or be targeted granularly, limiting scale outside Q4.

quote.text: they don't have enough traffic to guarantee that you're able to spend your whole budget.
quote.speaker: Spencer

warnings.warning: Heavy seasonality: growth that relies on holiday sales or friends and family is not a sustainable traffic source.

quote.text: I call these like unsustainable sales, right?
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Sudden order surges can overwhelm operations; they had to turn off the Etsy shop in Q4 2020.

quote.text: There was a moment where we had to turn off the Etsy shop because we couldn't handle the influx of orders that were coming in.
quote.speaker: Spencer

warnings.warning: Old Instagram growth tactics (engagement pods, paid shout-outs on big pages) no longer work.

quote.text: All that doesn't work at all anymore
quote.speaker: Spencer

warnings.warning: Being dogmatic about hand-made differentiation may leave money on the table if customers just want cheaper.

quote.text: do we want to be like, dogmatic about our mission, or do we want to be profitable?
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Inventory-based products (sewn goods) brought sourcing and manufacturing headaches versus print-on-demand.

lessons.lesson: Print-on-demand plus commissioned offshore labour lets you start for almost nothing and stay cash-flow positive without inventory.

quote.text: I don't have to invest in inventory or anything like that. I was a pretty cashflow heavy business
quote.speaker: Spencer

lessons.lesson: Giftable products convert best around Black Friday and Christmas; plan cash and capacity for that peak.
To scale with paid ads in e-commerce you need roughly 60-70% gross margins.

quote.text: if you really want to push with paid ads, you kind of have to have a 60 to 70, you do, brose margin.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: On modern Meta ads, creative volume and freshness matter more than targeting.

quote.text: You just worry about creative and they'll find the people.
quote.speaker: Spencer

lessons.lesson: Test assumptions about what customers value (human vs AI art) directly instead of assuming.

quote.text: Because sometimes we assume like they want it to be drawn by a human.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Add-on upsells and a guided customiser lift order value substantially.
Early movers in new platform categories (TikTok Live auctions) get outsized algorithmic distribution.

quote.text: the first movers to any given category on TikTok are getting pushed like crazy any algorithm.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: AI image models now make offering cheap automated product variants and lead-gen visuals practical.
Entrepreneurs are constant students; YouTube can teach most tools within a week.

quote.text: I think one of the coolest things about entrepreneurship in general is you are a constant student
quote.speaker: Spencer

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand operator with fairly specific monthly revenue, margin and AOV numbers, but Whisper transcription garbles names and some figures (e.g. '$24,000' email list, profit numbers), and current performance is vaguely 'down'.
